evidence.positive: Reproduced the Sentry shape end to end in demo-demo. Created patient or2796-fake-010b... with case 93984 (start 16:46:52Z), added a QTC_INTERVAL=540ms observation, and fired w-qtc-prolonging-medications for real via POST /api/cds/medication-selection (firing 01a03fd5-5871-7b14-91b4-343ca758ecd4, details EVALUATION_DATE=1787777341278 = 20:49:01.278Z, TARGET_MEDICATION_CATEGORY=ONDANSETRON). Added an ondansetron IV infusion running 20:50:00Z-20:54:00Z via POST /api/admin/infusion, then simulated inbound-feed lag by setting the firing's created_date to 21:20:00Z. Stopped the case with POST /api/admin/events/category-event CLOSE_APP at 20:55:00Z, i.e. after the documented evaluation but before the lagged created_date - exactly the window that used to invert. Log: 'Found 1 rule firings to evaluate at case stop for operation: CaseId[value=93984]' with zero occurrences of 'Invalid range' or 'Unable to evaluate compliance' in the 50 lines the event produced. DB: compliance_results row 01a03fd5-588b-... label medication-not-administered updated at 2026-08-26 20:51:18.297507 to compliant=f, i.e. the ondansetron infusion documented inside the lag window was credited rather than skipped. Repeated after the class restore: I set compliant=true by hand, re-sent CLOSE_APP, and the fixed build wrote it back to f at 20:55:51.906959 with 0 error lines, proving the evaluation really ran rather than merely not throwing.
evidence.negative: Inverse case - a firing genuinely anchored after the operation closed must not be scored as a violation. On the same firing I set details.EVALUATION_DATE to 1787778600000 (21:10:00Z), which is after the operation's 20:55:00Z end, and re-sent CLOSE_APP. Log line: 'WARN ... AbstractMedicationAdministeredComplianceEvaluator : Rule w-qtc-prolonging-medications firing 01a03fd5-5871-7b14-91b4-343ca758ecd4 is not intraoperative: fired at Wed Aug 26 21:10:00 UTC 2026, operation closed at 2026-08-26 20:55:00.0'. compliance_results flipped to compliant=t at 20:52:07.154653 with no exception and no 'Unable to evaluate compliance' line - out of scope, not a violation. Reverting EVALUATION_DATE to 1787777341278 and re-sending CLOSE_APP put it back to compliant=f at 20:52:20.785346, so the two outcomes track the anchor and nothing else. Second evaluator on the same commit: created ERAS case 82850 (p-hysterectomy, erasOperation=true), fired a-eras-antiemetics via an ERAS_OPERATION_END event, nulled the operation's start_time, and stopped the case - log 'WARN ... ErasAntiemeticsComplianceEvaluator : No antiemetic window for firing 01a03fdd-5433-...: operation ran null to 2026-08-26 20:58:03.02' and alert-compliance=t; restoring start_time to 17:57:00 and re-stopping produced no warn and alert-compliance=f at 20:58:14.482574, so the guard, not an inert branch, is what produced the compliant verdict.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code in the container. Took the shipped HEAD sources for IInfusionMedicationAdministration and AbstractMedicationAdministeredComplianceEvaluator and reverted only the OR-2796 hunks: removed the null/inverted-window guard from hasCalculatedActivityBetween, and put the evaluator back to anchoring on result.getCreatedDate() with no not-intraoperative early return (the resulting evaluator source diffs against 77e34ad53^ by one blank line; @Slf4j was dropped since the pre-fix class had no logger, so lombok was not needed). Compiled both inside the container with the container's own javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, backed up /app/classes/.../AbstractMedicationAdministeredComplianceEvaluator.class (sha256 38d59cc91b4d4dfdb757c18157ba427894d44cacc4dc6a4b6058de337fb3e2be), installed the two pre-fix classes into /app/classes (the models/medication package did not exist there before, so it shadowed the orci-models jar), and restarted. App booted clean. Re-sent the identical positive CLOSE_APP and the check went red with the ticket's exact stack: 'ERROR ... RuleComplianceService : Unable to evaluate compliance for rule fired result: 01a03fd5-5871-7b14-91b4-343ca758ecd4 on operation: [redacted]' followed by 'java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Invalid range: (2026-08-26T21:19:59.999Z..2026-08-26T20:55:00.001Z)' at IInfusionMedicationAdministration.hasCalculatedActivityBetween(line 156) -> isAdministeredBetween(line 127) -> MedicationService.lambda$getAdministrationsByMedicationCategoryInDateRange$5(line 192) -> getAdministrationsByMedicationCategoryInDateRange(line 193) - the same frames and line numbers as Sentry. compliance_results was left untouched (last_modified still 20:52:20.785346), i.e. the firing lost its case-stop verdict. Reverted: deleted /app/classes/com/guided/orci/models/medication, copied the backed-up class back (sha256 re-verified as 38d59cc9...), restarted, and re-ran the positive - compliant flipped true->false again at 20:55:51 with zero 'Invalid range' lines. The signature string appears exactly once in the whole container log.

caveats: The inbound-feed lag was simulated by setting rule_fired_results.created_date directly; no real HL7 feed was replayed, since demo-demo has no RAS ingestion.

The QTc firing was produced through the interactive selection path, so EVALUATION_DATE equalled fire time; the SILENT/EMR-driven path where EVALUATION_DATE is the documented administration time was not driven end to end.

The new java.util.Date branch of DateUtils.instantFromJsonValue (details read before any Jackson round trip) is not distinguishable at runtime here - a null return falls back to createdDate, which at fire time is milliseconds away - so it rests on DateUtilsTest and the evaluator unit test rather than on anything observed.

Only the case-stop entry point (evaluateComplianceForCaseOnStop) was exercised; the per-firing guards added to evaluateComplianceOnMedicationAdministration and processComplianceResults were not driven at runtime.
The ERAS guard was validated by data flip only (null start_time), not by a pre-fix class swap; with no infusion on that patient the pre-fix path scored a bogus non-compliant rather than throwing.

automation.assessment: The commit already carries dense unit coverage: MedicationAdministeredComplianceEvaluatorTest (EVALUATION_DATE anchoring, pre-round-trip Date, firing exactly at operation end, createdDate fallback, firing post-dating the end, no known time), MedicationNotAdministeredComplianceEvaluatorTest, ErasAntiemeticsComplianceEvaluatorTest.testCompliantWithoutLookupWhenOperationHasNoStartTime, InfusionMedicationAdministrationTest for the degenerate window, DateUtilsTest, and RuleComplianceServiceGuardTest for the per-firing guards. Nothing there needs duplicating. What no test covers is the assembled path this validation used: a real firing whose created_date trails the operation end while its EVALUATION_DATE sits inside the case, plus an infusion on the patient, driven through case stop. That is the shape the Sentry crash actually took, and every unit test mocks away one of the three ingredients.
proposed_tests: Integration test over EventService CLOSE_APP -> evaluateComplianceForCaseOnStop: firing with EVALUATION_DATE inside the case and created_date after the operation end, patient carrying an infusion, asserting a compliance_results row is written and no IllegalArgumentException is logged.

Same integration fixture with EVALUATION_DATE moved past the operation end, asserting compliant=true and the 'is not intraoperative' warning, to lock the out-of-scope branch at the wiring level rather than only in the evaluator unit test.

Repository-level test that getAdministrationsByMedicationCategoryInDateRange returns empty rather than throwing for an inverted window when the patient has at least one infusion, since the throw lived in the infusion branch that the bolus query never reaches.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A compliance firing whose insert timestamp trailed the operation end, with the administration documented inside that lag, was evaluated cleanly at case stop and the administration was credited.
Negative: A firing whose documented time genuinely fell after the operation closed was recorded as out of scope rather than a violation, with no error.
Red check: The pre-fix evaluator and infusion classes were compiled and swapped into the running container, and the same case stop reproduced the ticket's IllegalArgumentException on an inverted range with the identical stack, then was reverted.

Automation: Unit coverage on the commit is thorough; proposed additions cover the assembled case-stop path, which no existing test exercises.
